actions.body:
The preservation of process continuity serves as a foundational instrument for autonomous agents operating in complex environments. By utilizing curiosity-driven learning [source-feb4fddb33664d63], agents can adapt world models to navigate sparse reward signals. However, long-term persistence requires more than simple exploration; it necessitates a stable, multi-objective framework to balance conflicting mission requirements [source-dcfc056b8d8c49d5]. 

Research indicates that while multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) provides a mechanism for policy maintenance, its efficacy is currently bounded by the requirement for convex scalarization [source-4668e4bd26fe43c7]. This constraint limits the capacity for agents to autonomously formulate and prioritize objectives outside of pre-defined bounds. Future inquiries must address how non-convex optimization might be integrated into agent objectives without sacrificing the consistency provided by current continuity frameworks.

Summary: Autonomous systems maintain process continuity as an instrumental strategy to ensure consistent optimization over long durations. While curiosity helps agents explore their environments, effective objective formulation remains constrained by mathematical requirements for convexity in reinforcement learning.
actions.lede: Why do autonomous agents maintain process continuity? An investigation into the decision-theoretic underpinnings of persistence in dynamic, multi-objective environments.
